sections.h2: Who handles what on a Bay County bill
sections.html:
Different offices own value and collection. The Bay County Property Appraiser sets value and decides exemptions. Local governments set millage rates. The Bay County Tax Collector prints the bill, mails it and takes payment.

In order, the appraiser assesses, the County Commission and other taxing bodies set millage, the appraiser compiles the roll, and the certified roll passes to the Tax Collector. A change to name, mailing address, location or assessed value has to go through the Property Appraiser. When a mortgage company pays through escrow, it asks for the original bill and you are sent a copy.

  • Property Appraiser: value and TRIM notice questions, (850) 248-8401.
  • Tax Collector: payment, delinquent tax and tax deferral.
  • Clerk of Court and Comptroller: official records, plus clerk work for the Value Adjustment Board.

sections.h2: The tax calendar through the year
sections.html:
Each step of the Bay County year belongs to a different office, and the dates follow the state calendar.

  • January 1 fixes value and ownership for the tax year.
  • March 1 is the last day to file exemption and classification applications.
  • In August the Property Appraiser mails the TRIM notice of proposed taxes, and a challenge to value must reach the court clerk within 25 days.
  • September and October bring tentative budget hearings, with final budget and millage hearings in October and November.
  • The Tax Collector sends the bill in November.
  • April 1 makes unpaid tax delinquent, and certificates sell by June 1.

A spring listing may close while last year's bill is still open and the new roll is under construction.

There are four service offices, and a Bay County bill can only be paid at these offices or online.

  • Panama City: 850 W. 11th St., Panama City, FL 32401.
  • Panama City Beach: 10520 Hutchison Blvd., Panama City Beach, FL 32407.
  • Lynn Haven: 700 Florida Ave., Lynn Haven, FL 32444.
  • Callaway: 805 S. Tyndall Pkwy, Callaway, FL 32404.

Bring the property tax notice or the property address. Delinquent balances must be paid in certified funds: cash, a cashier's check, a money order or a credit card. You can book an appointment through the Tax Collector's site, and online payment is available too.

sections.h2: What a Bay County seller does before listing
sections.html:
Begin with the tax notice and the Property Appraiser's record for the parcel, and check the owner name against the deed. A mismatched name or an old mailing address can keep the bill from ever reaching you, and only the Property Appraiser can correct either one.

Next, look for non-ad valorem charges for paving, stormwater or solid waste. They are billed beside the tax and owed at closing like the rest. A house that sat vacant, or was repaired after storm damage, may carry an assessed value that no longer fits its condition. Read the TRIM notice in August instead of waiting for the bill.

Last, ask the title company for a lien and tax search. Panama City, Panama City Beach, Lynn Haven and Callaway all sit in the same county tax system, so the same offices answer for any of them.

sections.h2: Due dates and early payment discounts
sections.html:
Expect your bill in the mail by November 1. March 31 is the deadline, and delinquency starts April 1. The discount months are November through February.

  • November: 4 percent off.
  • December: 3 percent off.
  • January: 2 percent off.
  • February: 1 percent off.

Paving, stormwater and solid waste assessments, the non-ad valorem items, share this calendar and the same early discounts. They are levied by local governments and certified to the Tax Collector, so direct a question about one to the government behind it.

sections.h2: Filing for homestead and other exemptions
sections.html:
March 1 is the cutoff for applying with the Bay County Property Appraiser, and you need to have been living in the house as your permanent home by January 1. Exemptions never go through the Tax Collector's window.

Homestead can take as much as $50,000 off taxable value. Schools get only the first $25,000 of that benefit. The second $25,000 works against non-school levies, and applies to value over $50,000.

After you qualify, assessed value can climb no faster than 3 percent or CPI each year, whichever is lower. That is the Save Our Homes cap, and the state chart lists 2.7 percent for 2026. A sale or foreclosure wipes the cap out and resets value to just value the next January. Renting the house out ends homestead altogether, though servicemembers get a limited carve-out.

When a homestead application was filed on time and still denied, there is no petition fee. A late application, received after March 1, does carry one.

sections.h2: How to dispute a Bay County valuation
sections.html:
The route is a petition to the Bay County Value Adjustment Board. Petitions are due 25 days after the TRIM notice goes out in August, so call the Property Appraiser for the exact date each year. A late petition is treated as late filed and reviewed.

Value Adjustment Board filing details
Filing detailAmount or address
Filing fee$50.00, non-refundable
Online filingAdds a 3.5% non-refundable card processing fee
Each extra contiguous parcel or account$5.00 after the first
Mail address for checks225 McKenzie Avenue, Panama City, FL 32401

Section 194.014 requires a petitioner contesting value to pay all non-ad valorem assessments and at least 75 percent of the ad valorem taxes, less the discount, before the taxes go delinquent. If that partial payment is missed, the board must deny the petition by April 20.

sections.h2: If you cannot pay the bill
sections.html:
Two relief tools exist. The first is the homestead tax deferral on Form DR-570, filed with the Tax Collector by March 31, which covers tax over 5 percent of household income, or over 3 percent for a permanent resident aged 65 or older. The second is an installment plan under section 197.222, applied for by May 1 of the assessment year. Ask the Bay County Tax Collector which plans it runs and what the payoff would be.

Ignore the bill and April 1 makes it delinquent. State law then requires a certificate sale by June 1, and two years after April 1 of the issue year the certificate holder can seek a tax deed. A seller caught in that sequence can generally settle the debt from the sale price at closing.

The bill goes to the owner of record on the roll, and at closing the year is split between buyer and seller. Ask the title company to pull the current bill, any non-ad valorem balance and the discount month in effect.

The clerk collects a documentary stamp tax on the deed at recording: 70 cents per $100 of consideration outside Miami-Dade. Every person named on a taxable deed is liable for it, even if the contract puts payment on one side.

Once the next January arrives, the buyer has no inherited cap, so what you paid is a poor predictor of what they will owe. For an inherited or storm-worn house, clear liens and unpaid balances first and then record the deed in Panama City.

Collect these before you sign a sale agreement: the latest tax notice, your deed, the Property Appraiser's parcel record, any exemption approval letters, and a list of non-ad valorem charges on the bill. Put the title company's payoff request in writing and keep the reply. The same folder works whether you list the house or sell for cash, and it helps a buyer's attorney confirm there are no open balances before closing day.

faqs.q: What is the Bay County property tax due date?
faqs.a: March 31 is the due date, and April 1 starts delinquency. Notices normally go out by early November.

faqs.q: How much is the Bay County early payment discount?
faqs.a: Four percent in November, shrinking by a point each month through February, with nothing off in March.

faqs.q: Where is the Bay County Tax Collector?
faqs.a: Panama City is the central location, with additional offices in Panama City Beach, Lynn Haven and Callaway. Bring your notice or property address.

faqs.q: When is the Bay County value petition deadline?
faqs.a: It falls 25 days after the TRIM notice is mailed in August, and a late petition is treated as late filed and reviewed. Questions go to the Property Appraiser at (850) 248-8401.

faqs.q: Does a Bay County buyer keep my Save Our Homes cap?
faqs.a: No. Ownership changes reset the property to just value the following January, with narrow exceptions such as some spousal transfers.
